title: AI-Assisted GWAS Analysis with Python
text:
Choose your route
Move from association tables to results you can check and explain. Learn with synthetic data, repeat the workflow with a published HDL-cholesterol study, then apply it to your own compatible summary statistics.
Start with Required setup. The shared workflow and reporting pages provide a reference once you know the steps.

title: AI-Assisted GWAS Analysis with Python
text:
What the figures answer

Manhattan and regional plots: where are the association signals?
Q–Q plots: how does the distribution compare with a simple reference?
Effect estimates and intervals: what are the direction, units and uncertainty?
Frequency, N and quality summaries: what supports each association and what was excluded?
Precision and p-value checks: are the quantities consistent with the declared source model?

Ten figure families are saved as PNG only. Every observation should be traced to a saved table. A variant row is not a participant; several associated variants are not automatically independent loci.
crumbs: 1  AI-Assisted GWAS Analysis with Python

title: AI-Assisted GWAS Analysis with Python
text:
Scope
This guide begins with processed autosomal, biallelic single-nucleotide, quantitative-trait beta summary statistics. It does not fit genotype association models, perform LD clumping, identify causal variants or predict individual risk. Odds ratios, sex chromosomes, indels and new study designs need explicit extensions.
AI can help explain an error or improve a draft. You define the question and supply the study context; scripts generate traceable evidence; you verify the arithmetic and decide which claims are justified.
Next: Set up your workspace
crumbs: 1  AI-Assisted GWAS Analysis with Python

title: Required setup
text:
Get the project and open the correct folder
Use the complete project ZIP supplied with the guide, or open the project repository and choose Code → Download ZIP. Extract it before working.
In VS Code choose File → Open Folder and select the folder containing _quarto.yml, requirements.txt, scripts/, data/ and examples/. Open Terminal → New Terminal there. If extraction produced an extra outer folder, open the inner project folder.
Run every guide command from this main project folder. On macOS/Linux, check with:

title: Required setup
text:
pwd
ls

title: Required setup
text:
Create a Python environment
Use Python 3.10 or later. The package resolver selects compatible dependency releases for your Python version; the reference run records the versions actually used.
On macOS/Linux:
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
On Windows PowerShell:
py -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
If PowerShell blocks activation, use Command Prompt and .venv\Scripts\activate.bat, or invoke .venv\Scripts\python.exe directly.
With the environment active:
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pip check
python -c "import numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, seaborn; print('Analysis packages loaded.')"
Matplotlib and Seaborn create the current static figures. Other listed packages support future data handling and exploration; installing them does not implement new methods. requirements-optional.txt is optional. See TOOLING.md for details.

title: Required setup
text:
Confirm the synthetic example works
python scripts/python/run_workflow.py --data-dir data/synthetic --output-dir results/synthetic --check-only
python scripts/python/run_workflow.py --data-dir data/synthetic --output-dir results/synthetic
python scripts/python/verify_variant.py data/synthetic results/synthetic SYN000001
The bundled input retains 15,760 of 22,000 rows. Each comparison printed by the verifier should agree. Reference variant beta is 0.12, SE is 0.02 and z is 6.
Synthetic inputs are already supplied. Run the following only if you intend to replace them with a regenerated version:
python scripts/python/prepare_synthetic.py
Keep input hashes and package versions; a seed alone does not guarantee identical files across all environments.

title: Required setup
text:
Render or preview the guide
Install Quarto separately from Python. Then:
quarto render
quarto preview
Open the preview address printed in the terminal. Press Ctrl+C to stop. Rendering displays saved images and commands; it does not execute the analysis.
If a plot in the guide differs from the one in results/, confirm you are in the correct repository, rerun the analysis, render again, then refresh the browser. _quarto.yml copies the figure resources into docs/.

title: Required setup
text:
Troubleshooting







Symptom
Next check




File not found
Confirm the project root and exact filename


Missing package
Activate the environment and reinstall requirements


Literal p-value zero
Obtain a valid source value or source log-p; do not invent a replacement


Very small positive p such as 1e-769
Keep it as text; the workflow computes its log without flooring


Missing INFO
Declare verified absence in metadata; no quality scores are fabricated


Large real-study run takes longer
The workflow reads all prepared variants and writes full compressed audit tables; allow it to finish

title: Run the workflow
text:
Define the analysis before running
Use this page after setup as a command reference. If this is your first run, follow synthetic practice in order.
Record the trait, source, population descriptors, genome build, effect allele and effect units. Decide whether the input contains genome-wide background associations or only selected variants. The latter cannot support global Q–Q or lambda diagnostics.
The workflow checks prepared files; it cannot establish that source allele orientation, phenotype processing or upstream model adjustment was correct.

title: Run the workflow
text:
Parameters are visible
config/default.json contains the reference p-value, minimum MAF, minimum INFO, number of rows in the effect plot and maximum plotted background points. Change a copy of this file when needed:
python scripts/python/run_workflow.py --data-dir data/my-study --output-dir results/my-study --config config/my-study.json
The default INFO filter is applied only when metadata declares INFO available. For GLGC, it is explicitly not applied. The GLGC frequency filter uses the supplied reference-panel frequency, not a fabricated study frequency.

title: Run the workflow
section: Large files: analysis and display are different
text:
Large files: analysis and display are different
All valid prepared rows enter QC and all retained rows enter summaries, threshold counts, top-variant selection and lambda. Dense scatter plots show all retained p≤1e-5 rows plus a reproducible sample of at most 50,000 remaining background rows. The plotted rows are saved in scatter-display.tsv.
The Q–Q plot uses selected ranks from the full sorted p-value distribution. Its expectations and envelope use the full retained count. It does not recompute a Q–Q reference from a hits-enriched scatter sample.
For inputs exceeding 100,000 rows, full QC/results tables are compressed as .tsv.gz. Read them with a gzip-aware tool; do not edit them in a spreadsheet. PNGs and small display/summary tables remain easy to inspect.

title: Run the workflow
text:
Verify before explaining
Use the full table or the provided frozen verification rows, not a figure alone. Check a named variant, a filtering count and one figure observation. For the published example, source meta-analysis p-values legitimately differ from the derived normal Wald calculation.
The run record stores metadata, parameters, software versions, input and script hashes, and the plotting policy. Keep source-preparation notes with it. These records describe a run; they do not establish causal interpretation.
Next: Write the report

title: Write the report
text:
A practical structure
A report should answer the question, show the evidence and explain the limits of the analysis. Aim for a short account that another learner can reproduce.

title: Write the report
text:
Section
Include




Question and data
Trait, source/citation, variant counts, population, genome build and effect units


Methods
Preparation, exclusions, parameters, source test and display policy


Verification
Named variant, source p text, derived calculations and agreement checks


Results
Selected figures with checked values and source table names


Limitations
Relative to this source, selection, uncertainty, ancestry, LD and causal claims


Reproducibility
Commands, paths, input/code hashes, environment and analysis date

title: Write the report
text:
Create a report
Create reports/ if it does not exist. Save a plain-text QMD there, for example reports/synthetic-report.qmd. Start with the template in templates/ or the final lesson of the corresponding example. Replace every bracketed prompt.
quarto render reports/synthetic-report.qmd --to html
Paths in report templates start ../results/ because reports are one folder below the project root. A report does not have to be added to the book chapters in _quarto.yml to render on its own.

title: Write the report
text:
Choose figures for a reason
The workflow supplies ten figure families, but a report need not repeat them all. Use Manhattan and a regional view to describe location, Q–Q to discuss a distribution, an effect plot for direction/uncertainty, and QC diagnostics where they answer a question. Include a table when exact numbers matter more than a plot.
Example of checked wording: “SYN000001 had beta 0.12 per A allele relative to G, SE 0.02 and z=6. Its synthetic Wald p-value was approximately 1.97×10⁻⁹. This is a fictional calculation example.”
For GLGC, a p-value difference is not automatically an error: the source test is a corrected meta-analysis, whereas the displayed beta/SE check is an approximate normal Wald calculation.

title: Write the report
text:
Use AI with evidence
A useful prompt is: “Using only these checked variant values and source-method notes, draft a concise descriptive result. Name the effect allele and units. Separate numerical evidence from claims requiring LD, replication or causal analysis.”
Review every number, allele, citation and limitation. Do not accept invented gene names, independent-locus counts or clinical recommendations.

title: Write the report
text:
Final review

Do the figure, input version, table and report all refer to the same run?
Are exact source p-values preserved when they are below ordinary floating-point range?
Are reference frequencies and unavailable INFO clearly described?
Is a count of associated variants distinguished from independent loci?
Are selection bias and nominal confidence intervals acknowledged?

Learner reports are ignored by Git. Reusable templates, guide pages, scripts, inputs and published guide figures belong to the project.

title: Synthetic GWAS: start here
text:
What this version teaches
The bundled file contains 22,000 fictional variant rows across 22 autosomes. No real people, genotypes, rsIDs or biological gene assignments are included. sample_size is a simulated per-variant value concentrated near a nominal maximum of 20,000, with a smaller lower-coverage component; it is not the number of variants.
The generator uses varied invented chromosome spans and marker densities, a low-frequency/common-variant mixture, and three locally denser signal regions. Local latent noise is correlated by distance. INFO and coverage can be lower for lower-frequency variants, and SE depends on N, frequency and INFO. It also includes a fixed reference variant. These are teaching mechanisms, not a real LD reference or a fitted GWAS model. Filtering retains 15,760 variants for the bundled input version.
Follow the seven pages in order, using the same setup, analysis and verification commands throughout.
Next: Preview the results
Most variants have N close to 20,000; a smaller component has lower coverage. The frequency histogram no longer assumes a uniform distribution. These choices create useful diagnostic patterns, without claiming to reproduce a specific population or trait.
The fixed reference is an intentional exception to the simulated SE formula. Its beta, SE, EAF, INFO, N and allele pair are preserved for verification.

title: Preview the results
text:
Manhattan plot
All ten figures below come from the bundled synthetic inputs. Every figure is marked synthetic. Numerical values live in results/synthetic/tables/.
Question: Where are the strongest associations?
Each point is a retained variant. Autosomes alternate contrasting dark blue and orange; these colours distinguish chromosomes and do not encode effect direction or significance; the dashed line marks the configured reference p-value. Several nearby points do not establish several independent loci.

title: Preview the results
text: Manhattan plot: synthetic GWAS summary-statistics example.

title: Preview the results
text:
Q–Q plot
Question: How do observed p-values compare with a simple null reference?



Q–Q plot: synthetic GWAS summary-statistics example.


Observed and expected −log10 p-values use all retained variants. The left panel shows the full tail and the right magnifies the central distribution using the same variants. The envelope is 95% pointwise under independent Uniform(0,1) p-values. Correlated variants and true signals limit this reference; it is neither simultaneous nor LD-adjusted.

title: Preview the results
text:
Effect estimates and intervals
Question: What direction and uncertainty do the smallest-p variants have?



Effect estimates and intervals: synthetic GWAS summary-statistics example.


Row labels include variant ID, chromosome, position, and effect/other alleles. Beta is per copy of the named effect allele, relative to the other allele. Nearby variants may have opposite signs because their named alleles differ; sign comparisons require allele context. Intervals are unadjusted 95% Wald intervals for variants selected by p-value. They are subject to selection bias and are not independent-locus estimates.

title: Preview the results
text:
Frequency and imputation quality
Question: What measurements are being filtered?



Frequency and imputation quality: synthetic GWAS summary-statistics example.


The panels show minor allele frequency and INFO distributions. Input and retained MAF histograms use identical bin edges. The low-frequency/common mixture is a teaching choice, not an empirical population estimate. Thresholds are teaching defaults, not universal quality rules. INFO definitions can vary by source pipeline.

title: Preview the results
text:
Effect versus frequency
Question: How do estimated effects vary across allele frequencies?



Effect versus frequency: synthetic GWAS summary-statistics example.


Orange points meet the configured p-value reference. Low-frequency estimates can have different precision. This plot does not establish a biological relationship between frequency and effect.

title: Preview the results
text:
Per-variant sample size
Question: How much data supports each association?



Per-variant sample size: synthetic GWAS summary-statistics example.


The synthetic distribution has most variants near nominal N=20,000 and a smaller lower-coverage tail. In real sources, variant-specific N can differ because of missingness or contributing cohorts. Counting variant rows does not count participants. Effective N and actual N must not be conflated when importing studies.

title: Preview the results
text:
Filtering audit
Question: How many variants remain after each step?



Filtering audit: synthetic GWAS summary-statistics example.


Counts and percentages apply MAF first, then INFO. Percentages excluded at each step use the previous step as denominator. A variant failing both criteria is removed once. Invalid inputs stop the run; they are not silently discarded.

title: Preview the results
text:
Position-only association zoom
Question: What surrounds the smallest p-value?



Position-only association zoom: synthetic GWAS summary-statistics example.


This plot uses ±250 kb around the retained variant with smallest p-value. It has no LD colours, gene tracks or fine-mapping probabilities. Synthetic positions have no biological mapping.

title: Preview the results
text:
Precision versus sample size
Question: why does higher N not guarantee that every variant has a smaller SE?



Standard error versus per-variant N, coloured by MAF; SE uses a log scale.


SE depends jointly on N, frequency and INFO in this simulation. Colours provide frequency context; this scatter is not a fitted model or a causal test. The fixed reference row is an intentional exception to the simulated formula. Numerical evidence is in precision-display.tsv.

title: Preview the results
text:
Source versus derived Wald p-values
Question: do the supplied p-values agree with the beta/SE-derived normal test?



Source versus derived Wald association strength, with a difference panel.


Here, source p-values were generated by the same normal Wald formula, so near-perfect agreement is expected. The maximum difference in −log10(p) is about 3.3×10⁻¹³, consistent with numerical rounding. The difference panel retains a visible scale instead of magnifying that rounding into an apparent substantive discrepancy. These are arithmetic checks, not independent biological validation. Real source tests can differ legitimately; preserve their p-values and inspect the study methods.
Your task: choose one checked observation for each figure. Explain why a cluster of top variants does not identify independent loci, and why synthetic plots cannot establish a biological finding.
Next: Meet the data

title: Meet the data
text:
data/synthetic/summary-statistics.tsv has one variant association per row. study-metadata.json describes the study context. This is a simplified teaching contract, not a claim of full GWAS-SSF compliance. Keep original files when mapping a source into this format.







Field
Meaning / required constraint




variant_id
Unique source identifier; synthetic IDs begin SYN


chromosome
Integer autosome 1–22


position
Positive integer coordinate in the declared build


effect_allele
Single uppercase A/C/G/T base to which beta refers


other_allele
Distinct comparison allele


beta
Quantitative-trait effect estimate per effect allele


standard_error
Positive standard error on the same beta scale


p_value
Source association p-value, strictly greater than 0 and at most 1


effect_allele_frequency
Frequency of the effect allele, between 0 and 1


sample_size
Positive simulated per-variant N


imputation_info
Source imputation score between 0 and 1



The metadata records trait, effect units, population, build, source, synthetic status and whether the file is genome-wide or contains selected variants. Missing required measurements must not be invented. A different file may need an explicit importer or an extended analysis contract.
For synthetic inputs the build is SYNTHETIC: coordinates and IDs are invented, even though chromosome numbers resemble real autosomes. No genome annotation is justified.
Palindromic A/T and C/G allele pairs are flagged. They are retained within this single-study inspection; a flag is not evidence that alleles are harmonized across studies. Multi-study harmonization requires source strands, frequencies, build and allele normalization.
Inspect the first rows in your editor. Locate SYN000001 and confirm beta 0.12, standard error 0.02, effect allele A, other allele G, EAF 0.25, N 20,000 and INFO 0.98.
Next: Check the inputs
The two input files are a simplified teaching contract. The real GLGC example uses the same core fields with explicitly declared reference frequency, source-reported N and unavailable INFO. Do not copy those declarations into a new study without verifying them against its source.

title: Check the inputs
text:
Filtering is explicit
Run from the project root:
For the bundled version expect:
Checks reject missing required cells, duplicate IDs/coordinates, unsupported alleles, nonfinite values, invalid p-values, nonpositive standard errors, invalid frequency/INFO ranges and inconsistent metadata. The starter supports one biallelic SNV record per genomic position.
Formatting checks cannot establish correct source allele orientation, build, ancestry adjustment, phenotype definition or model validity. Confirm these against study documentation.
config/default.json sets MAF ≥0.01 and INFO ≥0.8. MAF is min(EAF, 1−EAF). These are visible teaching defaults. Record any change and justify it from the study; no filtering is based on p-values.
--check-only checks and counts but does not create or refresh results. Invalid rows cause an error. Valid rows failing configured MAF/INFO filters are recorded in the full-run QC table.
Next: Run the analysis

title: Run the analysis
text:
Outputs to inspect
The command overwrites named results in results/synthetic/. Preserve separate folders when comparing configurations.
Ten PNG figures are saved under figures/. The preview explains each one.

title: Run the analysis
text:
Calculations and limits
The workflow preserves source p-values. It also derives \(z=\beta/SE\) and a two-sided normal Wald p-value for comparison; these need not match p-values from other source models. A discrepancy is a reason to inspect model definitions, not overwrite source results.
The default reference is p≤5×10⁻⁸. This is configurable and does not replace a study-specific multiple-testing plan. It does not identify independent loci. A 0.05/number-of-bundled-rows calculation is not substituted for a genome-wide threshold.
Lambda GC is median chi-square(1) transformed from source p-values, divided by the chi-square(1) null median. It is a diagnostic, not proof of confounding or good calibration, and no genomic-control correction is applied. Q–Q and lambda are skipped for metadata declaring selected_variants.
Next: Verify and explain

title: Run the analysis
text:
Figure files
Each figure is saved once as PNG. On rerun, the workflow removes old PDF/SVG exports for its ten known figure names in the selected output folder.
The Manhattan plot alternates dark blue and orange across autosomes. These colours distinguish neighbouring chromosomes; they do not encode significance or effect direction. The dashed grey line shows the p-value reference.
The Q–Q figure includes full-tail and central views. Forest labels include position and effect/other alleles; they do not identify independent loci.
Large-file display policies are shared with the real case study. All 15,760 synthetic retained rows are displayed because this dataset is below the background cap. Source p-values remain text; the engine saves source and derived Wald log strengths separately. Shared workflow explains the full-file calculations and large-file outputs.

title: Verify and explain
text:
Recalculate a named variant
For SYN000001, beta is 0.12 and SE is 0.02, so \(z=6\). Its approximate reference values are:
The verifier uses math.erfc and statistics.NormalDist rather than the workflow’s SciPy calculations. Every comparison should print agrees=True. It checks a retained row; excluded variants remain in variant-qc.tsv.

title: Verify and explain
section: Trace a figure to its evidence
text:
Trace a figure to its evidence

Compare the Manhattan peaks with variant-results.tsv. Count variants below the p reference; do not call that the number of independent loci.
Open top-variants.tsv. Check whether several entries are near one another on a chromosome.
Compare input, after-MAF and retained counts in filter-summary.tsv.
Read lambda and its definition in analysis-summary.json. Explain why simulated true signals and correlation affect interpretation.
Confirm that the position zoom has no LD estimates or gene assignments.

Evidence sentence: “For fictional variant SYN000001, beta was 0.12 per A allele relative to G, with an unadjusted 95% Wald interval of 0.0808–0.1592 and p≈1.97×10⁻⁹. These simulated results demonstrate calculation and do not support a biological claim.”
Use AI to improve the explanation only after supplying the checked values, allele definitions and synthetic status.

title: Write the report
text:
Create a reports/ folder. Save a new file as reports/synthetic-report.qmd. Copy the template below and complete each bracketed prompt with checked evidence. A ready-to-copy version is also in templates/synthetic-report.qmd.
---
title: "Synthetic GWAS: checked summary-statistics report"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
---

## Question and data

I inspected 22,000 fictional quantitative-trait variant associations across
22 simulated autosomes. These are synthetic summaries, not real participants
or fitted genotype associations. The configured filters retained 15,760 rows.

## Methods

I checked the required fields and study metadata, then applied MAF ≥0.01
and INFO ≥0.8. I preserved source p-values, calculated beta/SE and 95% Wald
intervals, and used p≤5×10⁻⁸ as a configurable reference. I used the documented low-frequency/common mixture, varied invented chromosome
spans and a main high-coverage component with a smaller coverage tail. No LD clumping,
causal inference, genotype QC or association model fitting was performed.

## Verification

SYN000001 had beta 0.12 per A allele relative to G, SE 0.02, z=6,
two-sided Wald p≈1.97317529×10⁻⁹, and 95% interval 0.08080072–0.15919928.
[Record whether the independent verifier agreed.]

## Results

![Synthetic Manhattan plot.](../results/synthetic/figures/manhattan.png)

[Quote one checked association and distinguish variants from independent loci.]

![Synthetic Q–Q plot with an independent-null pointwise envelope.](../results/synthetic/figures/qq.png)

[Describe the pattern and explain the limits of lambda and the envelope.]

![Selected effect estimates and unadjusted 95% intervals.](../results/synthetic/figures/effect-forest.png)

[Name effect alleles and explain selection bias.]

![Sequential variant filtering counts.](../results/synthetic/figures/filter-audit.png)

[Quote before/after counts from filter-summary.tsv.]

### Additional diagnostics

![SE versus sample size with frequency context.](../results/synthetic/figures/precision-sample-size.png)

[Describe N, frequency and precision together; the reference row is an exception.]

![Source and derived normal Wald p-values.](../results/synthetic/figures/p-consistency.png)

The source p-values use the same formula as the derived test, so differences
of about 3.3×10⁻¹³ on the −log10 scale are numerical rounding, not independent
biological confirmation.

## Limitations and next checks

All data and coordinates are fictional. Neighbour correlation is simulated,
not an LD reference. Top variants are not independent loci or causal findings.
Intervals are unadjusted and selected by p-value. The Q–Q envelope assumes
independent uniform null p-values and is not simultaneous or LD-adjusted.
[State one useful next check.]

## Reproducibility

Inputs: data/synthetic/.
Parameters: config/default.json.
Outputs, input hashes and versions: results/synthetic/tables/run-record.json.
[Record the analysis date and code version.]
Render from the project root:
quarto render reports/synthetic-report.qmd --to html
Verify that all six referenced figures display and remove unfinished prompts before sharing. The other four figures can be added when they support a specific observation. Learner reports belong in the ignored reports/ folder; the reusable template remains versioned.
Next: The published GLGC study

title: GLGC HDL: a published human GWAS
text:
The data path
This example analyses the joint GWAS and Metabochip HDL-cholesterol release from the Global Lipids Genetics Consortium (Willer et al. 2013; Global Lipids Genetics Consortium n.d.). It is a full genome-wide association file, not a short list of published hits.
Preparation excludes 186,081 rows whose reference frequency is unavailable. The analysis then excludes 203,281 rows below the frequency threshold. These are variant counts, not participant counts. No source rows were selected because of their p-values.

title: GLGC HDL: a published human GWAS
section: Three important differences from synthetic practice
text:
Three important differences from synthetic practice

Frequency is from a reference panel. It describes 1000 Genomes EUR A1 frequency, not measured frequency across all meta-analysis participants.
INFO is unavailable. The guide does not invent scores; its INFO filter is explicitly not applied.
Source p-values are meta-analysis results. A derived beta/SE Wald value is a check on a different calculation and need not reproduce them.

A1 is coded as the trait-increasing allele in this release. Its nonnegative betas do not mean all possible allele substitutions increase HDL.
The authors’ association models and meta-analysis are upstream of this guide. We inspect their released summaries; we do not repeat participant QC, refit the models, count LD-independent loci or make causal/clinical claims.
Next: Preview the results




Global Lipids Genetics Consortium. n.d. “Global Lipids Genetics Consortium Results (2013).” Accessed November 27, 2026. https://csg.sph.umich.edu/willer/public/lipids2013/.

title: Preview the GLGC results
text:
Association landscape
The figures below come from the verified HDL release and the documented preparation/filtering steps. Read them alongside results/glgc-hdl/tables/. Ten PNG figure families answer different questions.
Autosomes alternate dark blue and orange. The strongest retained source association is rs247616, chromosome 16 at 56,989,590 on GRCh37, with p=1.15e-802. A full-range panel preserves that extreme value; the detail panel makes weaker signals visible. Triangles mark values above the detail panel’s display limit. Neither panel alters source values.
The plot contains all retained rows with p≤1e-5 plus 50,000 reproducibly sampled background rows. Calculations and the count of 3,285 variants at p≤5e-8 use all 2,058,079 retained rows. Do not count visible dots or interpret 3,285 as independent loci.

title: Preview the GLGC results
text: GLGC HDL Manhattan plot with the full association range and a 0–50 detail view.

title: Preview the GLGC results
text:
Distribution of p-values



Full-tail and central GLGC HDL Q–Q views.


The upper tail departs strongly from the simple reference. Lambda GC is 1.018789 for the retained file. These are post-release diagnostics: the source already used genomic control, and the joint design includes a custom array. A lambda near one does not prove absence of confounding or complete calibration.
Plot ranks are drawn from the full sorted retained file, and expected values use its full count. The shaded band assumes independent uniform null p-values; it is pointwise, not simultaneous or LD-adjusted.

title: Preview the GLGC results
text:
Selected effect estimates



Top retained source associations, with positions, effect/other alleles and nominal 95% Wald intervals.


The top twelve rows cluster on chromosome 16. This demonstrates why twelve small-p variants need not be twelve distinct findings. A1 is the increasing allele in this release, so the displayed betas are positive. Their units are the transformed HDL trait scale, not mg/dL. Intervals are derived as beta ±1.96×SE; they do not recreate the corrected meta-analysis test or adjust for selecting top rows.

title: Preview the GLGC results
text:
Frequency and unavailable quality information



Reference-frequency distributions and an explicit notice that INFO was not supplied.


Input and retained histograms use identical bins. The frequency filter uses 1000 Genomes EUR reference MAF. The right panel intentionally reports unavailable INFO instead of inventing a distribution. Absence of this field does not establish either good or poor imputation quality.

title: Preview the GLGC results
text:
Effect and frequency



Source beta versus reference-panel minor allele frequency.


Orange points meet the configured source p-value reference. Most smaller effects sit near zero, while some larger effects are visible. The plot is not an estimate of genetic architecture: effect coding, precision, source ascertainment and the display sample matter.

title: Preview the GLGC results
text:
Per-variant support



Distribution of the source-reported per-variant N values.


N varies across variants as contributing data differ. The source includes some decimal N values; they are preserved as reported. Do not round them into invented participant counts or assume they are effective N without source confirmation.

title: Preview the GLGC results
text:
Filtering audit



Sequential counts for reference-frequency filtering, with INFO explicitly not applied.


203,281 prepared rows (8.99%) fail the reference MAF threshold. The third stage removes none because INFO is unavailable. The separate source-preparation audit accounts for the earlier 186,081 rows with unavailable reference frequency.

title: Preview the GLGC results
text:
Precision with frequency context



Standard error versus source-reported N, coloured by reference MAF.


SE varies at similar N. Reference frequency provides useful context, but it is not the study frequency and this scatter does not fit a precision model. Source meta-analysis methods and contributing cohorts also affect interpretation.

title: Preview the GLGC results
section: Source p-values versus a derived Wald calculation
text:
Source p-values versus a derived Wald calculation



Source association strength compared with the beta/SE-derived normal Wald calculation.


These values do not agree as closely as in synthetic practice. That is expected: the paper describes a weighted Stouffer meta-analysis and genomic control, whereas the check uses the reported beta divided by its SE (Willer et al. 2013). Do not overwrite source p-values with the derived values to force agreement.
For rs3764261, source −log10(p) is 768.856985, while derived Wald −log10(p) is 832.466119. Both can be calculated correctly while answering different statistical questions.

title: Preview the GLGC results
text:
Regional position view



Retained associations within 250 kb of rs247616 on chromosome 16.


This view contains 430 retained variants. It locates a strong association cluster but supplies no LD colours, causal probabilities or gene assignments. Build-matched annotation and suitable LD data would be separate follow-up inputs.

title: Check the GLGC inputs
text:
Understand the exclusions
Preparation and analysis are different stages. The 186,081 unavailable-frequency exclusions belong to the importer audit. The analysis applies reference MAF ≥0.01 to the remaining rows, removing 203,281 more.
INFO is declared unavailable, so its threshold is not applied. The empty quality panel is an explicit limitation, not evidence that every variant passes an imputation-quality test. If a different source supplies valid INFO, keep it and apply a justified setting.

---
title: "GLGC HDL: checked summary-statistics analysis"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
---

## Question and source

I inspected the joint GWAS/Metabochip HDL-cholesterol release from
Willer et al. (2013), doi:10.1038/ng.2797. Prepared coordinates use GRCh37.
The authors' source: https://csg.sph.umich.edu/willer/public/lipids2013/.
I examined association summaries, not participant-level genotypes.

## Preparation and methods

The source had 2,447,441 variant rows. Preparation excluded 186,081 with
unavailable reference frequency, leaving 2,261,360. Reference MAF ≥0.01
retained 2,058,079. Frequencies come from 1000 Genomes EUR, not the complete
study sample. INFO was unavailable and its filter was not applied.

Source p-values, including very small positive values, were preserved as
text. I inspected source associations and derived separate normal Wald
quantities from beta/SE. The source uses corrected meta-analysis results;
these need not equal the derived calculation. Beta units are transformed
HDL units per A1 allele, not mg/dL. A1 is coded as increasing HDL.

Dense scatter plots show all retained p≤1e-5 rows plus 50,000 other rows.
Summary counts and lambda use the full retained file. Q–Q expectations
use the full count; the pointwise band assumes an independent null.

## Verification

rs3764261 had A/C, beta 0.2412, SE 0.0039, z=61.8461538462,
source p=1.39e-769, source −log10(p)=768.8569852 and derived normal
Wald −log10(p)=832.466118689. Its derived nominal 95% interval was
0.2335561405–0.2488438595. Reference MAF was 0.2942.
[Record whether the independent verifier agreed with saved quantities.]

## Results

![Source association landscape with a detail view.](../results/glgc-hdl/figures/manhattan.png)

The smallest retained source p-value was 1.15e-802 for rs247616 on
chromosome 16 at 56,989,590. There were 3,285 retained variants at p≤5e-8.
This is not a count of independent loci.
[Add one checked observation from a different region.]

![Full-tail and central Q–Q views.](../results/glgc-hdl/figures/qq.png)

The tail departed strongly from the simple reference; lambda GC for the
retained source file was 1.018789. This release already used genomic control,
and the diagnostic does not prove absence of confounding.

![Selected effect estimates and nominal intervals.](../results/glgc-hdl/figures/effect-forest.png)

[Describe allele coding, transformed units and the nearby positions.]

![Source-versus-derived p-value diagnostics.](../results/glgc-hdl/figures/p-consistency.png)

The source and derived tests differ. I retained the source p-values and
used the paper's meta-analysis methods to interpret the discrepancy.

![Reference frequency and unavailable INFO.](../results/glgc-hdl/figures/frequency-info.png)

[Describe the reference-frequency restriction and the unavailable quality field.]

## Limitations and next step

The analysis uses released summaries and a reference-frequency restriction.
It does not repeat the original participant QC, adjustment or meta-analysis.
Nominal intervals are derived from reported beta/SE and are unadjusted for
selecting top rows. No LD clumping, fine mapping, causal-gene assignment,
clinical-risk prediction or causal effect of HDL was established.
[Propose one next analysis with the additional inputs it would require.]

## Reproducibility

Inputs: data/glgc-hdl/. Outputs: results/glgc-hdl/.
Preparation: scripts/python/prepare_glgc.py.
Audit: data/provenance/glgc-hdl/preparation-audit.json.
Parameters, hashes and versions: results/glgc-hdl/tables/run-record.json.
[Record analysis date and code version.]
Render from the project root:
quarto render reports/glgc-hdl-report.qmd --to html
Open the HTML and check all five figure paths. Confirm that the report distinguishes source and derived p-values, reference and study frequencies, variant counts and independent loci. The source paper covers more than this lesson; do not claim to reproduce its entire discovery, fine-mapping or biological analysis.
Keep the learner report in ignored reports/. Retain the source citation, exact input version and source-preparation audit with any shared result.
Next: Your own study

title: Prepare your inputs
text:
The data contract
Create data/my-study/summary-statistics.tsv (or .tsv.gz) and study-metadata.json. Keep original files and a reproducible column-mapping/preparation record.
Metadata must declare study ID, trait, population, build, quantitative beta, effect units, file scope, source and synthetic status. A starter is supplied in templates/study-metadata.json.
Optional declarations have specific meanings:

title: Prepare your inputs
text:
Field
Required meaning




variant_id
Unique identifier traceable to the source


chromosome, position
Integer autosome 1–22 and positive coordinate in the declared build


effect_allele, other_allele
Distinct uppercase A/C/G/T bases


beta, standard_error
Quantitative-trait estimate and positive SE on the same scale


p_value
Positive source probability ≤1, preserved as text when needed


effect_allele_frequency
Frequency of the named effect allele; state study or reference basis


sample_size
Source-reported positive per-variant N


imputation_info
Valid source score in [0,1], when available






info_available: false: verified source absence; INFO is not filtered. Omit its column or use NA throughout. Do not fill it with 1.
frequency_basis: describe reference-panel frequency if that is what the source supplies.
sample_size_type: source_reported: preserve verified source non-integer N. Do not use this to hide malformed data or infer an unknown effective-N definition.
summary_scope: selected_variants: suppress global Q–Q/lambda. This does not recover omitted background variants.

title: Prepare your inputs
text:
Resolve source issues explicitly
Keep source p-values even when a different normal test can be derived from beta/SE. Literal zero is not a valid recovered probability; obtain source log-p or higher-precision values instead of inserting a floor. Extreme positive scientific notation is supported.
Resolve missing frequencies, multiple records at a coordinate, ambiguous allele orientation and unsupported variant classes upstream. Record exclusion reasons and counts. This is a teaching contract, not a complete GWAS-SSF importer (GWAS Catalog n.d.).

text: Vocabulary for reading a GWAS table

title: Appendix A — Appendix
text:
Term
Meaning here




Variant row
An association summary for a genomic variant, not a participant


Genome build
Coordinate reference; positions from different builds are not interchangeable


Effect allele
The allele to which beta and its frequency refer; not automatically minor, reference or harmful


Beta
Change on the stated quantitative-trait scale per copy of the effect allele


SE
Standard error on the beta scale


Source p-value
The released association-test result, retained separately from derived checks


EAF / MAF
Effect-allele frequency / smaller of EAF and 1−EAF


INFO
A source-defined imputation-quality metric when supplied


LD
Correlation among variants; position alone does not measure it


Locus / causal gene
A regional or biological interpretation requiring more than a list of small-p rows

title: Appendix A — Appendix
text:
Reference arithmetic
For a quantitative beta estimate and positive SE:
\[
z=\frac{\beta}{SE},\qquad CI_{95\%}=\beta\pm 1.959964\,SE.
\]
The derived two-sided normal Wald p-value is \(2\Phi(-|z|)\). It does not establish which test produced a source p-value. Preserve source methods and source values.
The plotted strength is \(-\log_{10}(p)\). Smaller p produces a higher point, not necessarily a larger effect. Precision and sample support influence significance.

The synthetic source uses the same normal formula. The GLGC source uses corrected meta-analysis results (Willer et al. 2013; Global Lipids Genetics Consortium n.d.). Both rows illustrate correct arithmetic; they do not imply the same test definition.

Very small positive p-values
Binary64 cannot represent every probability in a released GWAS file. The guide retains source p-value strings, using decimal logarithms for extreme values. Thus 1.39e-769 remains a positive source result; it is not replaced by zero or floored at an arbitrary minimum. Read p_value as text when independently inspecting such rows.
The verifier uses a stable normal-tail approximation for large z. An ordinary floating-point Wald probability may underflow, while its log remains finite. Compare named log quantities and state their test definitions.

title: Appendix A — Appendix
section: Frequencies, support and missing quality fields
text:
Frequencies, support and missing quality fields
MAF is \(\min(EAF,1-EAF)\). Changing the named allele reverses beta and replaces EAF by 1−EAF when the allele pair is properly aligned. It does not change MAF or a two-sided normal test.
Reference-panel frequency is not the frequency measured in every study cohort. The GLGC release supplies 1000 Genomes EUR frequency; the guide labels its basis and records exclusions for unavailable values. Other sources require their own documentation.
N is a per-variant source field, not the number of association rows. Some GLGC N values contain decimals; the guide preserves reported values without claiming why they are non-integer. It does not assume actual N and effective N are interchangeable.
If INFO is absent, metadata explicitly declares that absence and the filter is not applied. A missing distribution is not evidence of good imputation. Never fill an absent quality field with 1 merely to pass validation.

title: Appendix A — Appendix
text:
Filtering and display
The importer audit describes source-to-prepared transformations. The workflow audit describes MAF/INFO filtering of prepared rows. Their denominators differ; report both.
Summary calculations use every retained row. Dense scatters retain all p≤1e-5 rows and reproducibly sample at most 50,000 other background rows by default. The exact displayed rows and policy are recorded. Do not estimate variant counts from visible dots.
For Q–Q, ranks are selected from the full sorted distribution. With \(m\) retained rows and rank \(i\), the reference probability is \((i-0.5)/m\). The shaded interval uses beta order-statistic quantiles under independent uniform null p-values. It is pointwise, not a simultaneous or LD-adjusted band. Dense points need not imply independent tests.

title: Appendix A — Appendix
text:
Lambda and multiple testing
Lambda GC is the median chi-square(1) value transformed from source p-values divided by the chi-square(1) null median (Devlin and Roeder 1999). It is a diagnostic, not a correction applied by this guide or a proof of study validity. Source correction, true signal, sample size, variant selection, correlation and model issues influence interpretation.
The default p≤5×10⁻⁸ line is a declared reference for this worked example. A new study needs a justified multiple-testing plan. Threshold-crossing variants are not automatically independent loci, and a new threshold is not justified merely by counting a teaching subset.
A top-variant forest plot has selection bias and nearby rows may be correlated. Its nominal intervals are not simultaneous intervals or intervals adjusted for selection. The GLGC source test is not reconstructed by those intervals.

title: Appendix A — Appendix
text:
What requires additional evidence







Current result
Additional work before a stronger claim




A regional association cluster
Appropriate LD and study definitions before counting independent signals


A position near a gene
Build-matched annotation and biological evidence before causal-gene assignment


A small p-value
Effect units, source method, replication and study limits


A trait association
Separate causal design before an intervention or clinical conclusion


A useful synthetic demonstration
Verified real data before a biological finding



Summary-statistics QC benefits from source-level organization, explicit diagnostics and documented decisions (Winkler et al. 2014). The simplified TSV/JSON contract here is not a full GWAS-SSF validator (GWAS Catalog n.d.).

title: Appendix A — Appendix
text:
Reproducibility and scope
Keep prepared inputs, original source records, importer, parameters, analysis code, environment and report. SHA-256 hashes identify files; they do not validate scientific meaning. Version ranges and a run record do not constitute an exact portable environment lock.
The synthetic design is documented in data/provenance/SIMULATION-DESIGN.md. It uses invented coordinates, a frequency mixture, variable coverage and simulated local correlation. Its SE approximation is \([2N\,MAF(1-MAF)\,INFO]^{-1/2}\) except the fixed reference row. It supplies no empirical LD or genotype-model truth.
The real-data case inspects one published HDL release. It does not reproduce all lipid traits, original cohort QC, meta-analysis, LD analysis, enrichment or functional experiments from the paper.
